newsitem.title: USA: Alaska fund to pay $1,130 dividend to residents.
newsitem.headline: Alaska fund to pay $1,130 dividend to residents.

text.p: Each qualifying Alaska resident will receive an annual dividend of $1,130.30 from the Alaska Permanent Fund, officials said late Wednesday.
State Revenue Commissioner Wilson Condon, a member of the fund board of trustees, announced the record dividend at a banquet held during the organization's two-day annual meeting.
The dividend is the 15th annual payout to state residents from the 20-year-old fund, built with oil revenues and investment income.

Distribution of dividend checks is scheduled to start early next month. More than half the of recipients are expected to receive their payments in direct deposits to their bank accounts, fund officials said.
The total dividend payout will be $613.3 million, according to Permanent Fund financial reports.
Until this year, the highest dividend payout was the first, totaling $1,000 for each recipient. Last year's dividend was $990.30.
For fiscal year 1996, which ended June 30, the Permanent Fund posted a record $1.8 billion in earnings and $17.6 billion in assets, according to the annual report issued Wednesday.
Almost all year-round Alaskans, including children, are eligible to receive fund dividends. Alaska has about 600,000 residents.

Condon said the dividend has become important to Alaskans, accounting for 5 percent of the average Alaska family's disposable income and about 25 percent of the annual disposable income for the state's "least fortunate families."
Annual spending of dividend proceeds creates 8,000 jobs in the state, Condon said.
"For many of us, the dividend enriches our lives in many ways," he said.
